newsitem.title: USA: U.S. senator to offer bill to abolish Energy Dept.
newsitem.headline: U.S. senator to offer bill to abolish Energy Dept.

text.p: A Republican member of the Senate Energy Committee said Wednesday he will re-introduce a bill that stalled last session to abolish the Energy Department.

Sen. Rod Grams of Minnesota at a news conference also said he planned to question Federico Pena, President Clinton's choice to be the next energy secretary, on the justification for continuing the department.
The Senate Energy Committee is to hold a confirmation hearing on Pena Thursday.
Grams said the Energy Department has no apparent mission, and said the department has failed to carry out assigned tasks such as being ready to accept nuclear waste from states by 1998.
He also complained about its "bloated, bureaucracy laden, $16 billion annual budget."
Grams said his bill would create a three-year resolution agency to transfer "legitimate government functions" under the Energy Department's jurisdiction to other appropriate departments and agencies.
He said the bill would save an estimated $19-$23 billion over five years, and $5-$7 billion annually after that.

Grams' bill would transfer most basic science and civilian energy research functions to the Interior Department, transfer the three main defense laboratories to the Defense Department and set up a commission to consider closing remaining labs, send national security and environmental restoration and management activities to the Defense Department, and transfer civilian nuclear waste programs to the Army Corp of Engineers.
